business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Shipbuilding of Deep-Sea Dry Cargo and Container Vessels

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state company law or tax distinction applicable to the Proprietary Limited company)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Roman-Dutch common law with English company-law heritage, African customary law, and constitutional supremacy under the Constitution, 1996; unitary national Companies Act regime
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Protection of Investment Act 22 of 2015 read with s25 of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 (domestic investment protection framework)
South Africa-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 17 Dec 1997; in force 1 Apr 1998)
South Africa-Russia Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1998; in force 1999)
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment, Annex 1 (investment protection; in force for South Africa)
SACU Agreement 2002 (regional customs union context for maritime supply chains)
AfCFTA Investment Protocol (adopted Feb 2023; ratification pending)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008 ss 11, 13-14, 21-23, 50 and Companies Regulations 2011 regs 13-14 and 32-32D, as amended by the Companies Amendment Regulations 2023 (GN R3319, GG 48463), read with the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2023 (in force 27 Dec 2024); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 as amended by the FIC Amendment Act 1 of 2017 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act 12 of 2004.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - the CIPC beneficial-ownership register is accessible to the Financial Intelligence Centre, SARS, the National Prosecuting Authority, law-enforcement agencies and other competent authorities; it is not publicly searchable; nominee and shareholding arrangements must be disclosed in substance; the prescribed reporting threshold is 5%, stricter than the FATF default 25%.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each director and of each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the country of origin (South African Department of Home Affairs or foreign equivalent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or account-holding bank; certified by a South African notary or foreign notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / certificate of good conduct for each foreign director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal-record authority of the home country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry (CIPC for South African entities; foreign registries for foreign entities)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the South African incorporating agent or attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign principal executing before a notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference or good-standing letter for source-of-funds verification of founders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification with Hague Apostille where required under enhanced due diligence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors and beneficial owners against the FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions List (POCDATARA Schedule 4), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the South African domestic sanctions list maintained by the FIC; because the project involves USD/EUR trade finance and maritime installment letters of credit, OFAC SDN List and EU Consolidated List screening is also required in banking practice. Politically Exposed Persons trigger enhanced due diligence under FIC Guidance Note 7; the sector is treated as Medium_Risk_Enhanced under FIC Guidance Note 6 (risk-based approach) and Guidance Note 4A, requiring independent UBO verification, source-of-funds evidence, and trade-related red-flag review for dual-use maritime equipment.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_licensing_note_for_isic_3011: The enterprise requires statutory authorization and sectoral clearances before operations: South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA) vessel-registration and safety approvals, National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS) marine-equipment compliance, Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) environmental authorization for shipyard operations, and ITAC export-control assessment for ocean-going vessels and dual-use components; all such approvals are post-incorporation licenses but must be pre-verified during Stage 1 feasibility.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal - eservices.cipc.co.za; name reservation is lodged online under CIPC Name Reservation, Companies Act 71 of 2008 s11 and Companies Regulation 13.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed exclusively in Latin/Roman characters; non-Roman scripts are not accepted by the CIPC database. A name may be in English or any of the 11 official South African languages but must be recorded in Roman-script transliteration; for cross-border banking and maritime LC operations, an English rendering of the corporate name is mandatory in practice.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: South African or SA (where implying government connection)
SAS or defence-related expressions (subject to NCACC objection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: an application to extend a name reservation must be lodged with the CIPC before the reservation lapses, subject to the CIPC's discretion and the prescribed fee under Companies Regulation 13. Rejection appeal: upon CIPC refusal under s11(2) or s11(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, the applicant may either (a) file a fresh name-reservation application containing revised name tokens, or (b) within 15 business days of service of the CIPC rejection notice, apply to the Companies Tribunal under s160(1) as a person aggrieved, using Form CTR 110, attaching the CIPC rejection letter and a supporting affidavit; the Companies Tribunal may confirm, set aside or substitute the CIPC decision; any further aggrieved party may approach the High Court for judicial review under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. The registered office must be a physical street address in South Africa, not a post-office box, and serves as the domicilium citandi et executandi for service of process under s23(1) of the Companies Act. A law firm or accounting firm may provide the registered-office address virtually; however, because the enterprise is a shipyard carrying on physical manufacturing, a substantial operational premises in South Africa is mandatory and must be declared to CIPC and sectoral regulators. Virtual office services are therefore accepted solely for the statutory registered-address function.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 75% within the first three operating years). Unannounced on-site inspections are reasonably foreseeable by SARS (premises audits), the Department of Employment and Labour (OHS Act inspectors), the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (shipyard emissions, waste and water-use inspections), and SAMSA for vessels under construction; CIPC registered-office compliance checks occur at lower frequency. The Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML rating and dual-use export considerations increase the likelihood of regulatory site visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 – ss 13, 14, 15, 19, 66, 70 and 72; Companies Regulations, 2011 – Regs 12-18 and forms CoR 9.1, CoR 14.1, CoR 14.3, CoR 14.4 and CoR 15.1B; Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 and Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 for post-registration tax duties.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria; eServices portal: https://eservices.cipc.co.za
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CoR 14.1 – Notice of Incorporation, together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1B standard private-company MOI).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; a private company may have one or more shares of no par value and the MOI fixes authorised share capital. No government escrow account is required for incorporation; the escrow arrangement is a commercial-mandate step for maritime instalment payments and is created by the board resolution and banking mandate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Memorandum of Incorporation has been adopted, RESOLVED: 1. The subscription for shares set forth in the Memorandum of Incorporation is approved, and the allotment and issue of [number] ordinary shares to the founding subscribers is ratified with immediate effect. 2. The registered office is adopted at [full street address, City, Province, South Africa] for all statutory notices and legal service. 3. [Name(s)] is/are appointed as Director(s), [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each empowered to execute incorporation filings, banking mandates, and license applications. 4. The Chairperson is authorised to file the Notice of Incorporation with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, pay the prescribed fee, and take all ancillary steps. Adopted unanimously at [place and date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices – Online Name Reservation (Form CoR 9.1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC eServices portal and select 'Company Name Reservation'; complete Form CoR 9.1 with up to four proposed names ending in '(Pty) Ltd' for the commercial shipyard; pay the name reservation fee (approx. ZAR 50 per proposed name) by card; submit and download the Name Reservation Certificate, which remains valid for 60 business days.
required_dossiers: Identity document or passport of the applicant/incorporator
Notarised power of attorney where an agent lodges the application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is refused, file an amended CoR 9.1 within 20 business days; alternatively incorporate under an unreserved name and later apply to register the trading name through Form CoR 9.2 (Registration of Company Name) after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Signing and Certification of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators, first directors and a commissioner of oaths or notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI using standard Form CoR 15.1B or adopt a bespoke MOI compliant with the Companies Act; complete Form CoR 14.1 with company particulars; have each incorporator and director sign the consent to act (Form CoR 14.4); certify all identity documents before a commissioner of oaths; verify that no director is disqualified under section 69 of the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (Form CoR 14.4) for each director
Certified identity document or passport of each director and subscriber
Certified proof of residential address for non-resident directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any inconsistency between the MOI and Form CoR 14.1; re-attest defective signatures; where a director is disqualified under section 69, replace the director and file a new CoR 14.4 before lodgement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Incorporation Application to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create or update the CIPC customer profile on eservices.cipc.co.za; select 'Registration of Company'; upload scanned copies of the incorporation dossiers in PDF; pay the standard registration fee of approx. ZAR 175 (equivalent to USD 10); record the CIPC transaction reference number and download the Acknowledgment of Submission.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents and address proof
Payment confirmation and CIPC transaction reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC system queries missing or inconsistent documents, respond through the CIPC query portal within 10 business days with corrected forms; if the application is rejected, re-file Form CoR 14.1 with a corrected MOI and pay the applicable re-processing fee; escalate by calling the CIPC contact centre or through a Registered Application Agent (RAA).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Company Registration Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: CIPC verifies name availability and statutory compliance; upon approval the Registrar issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) bearing the unique South African registration number (format YYYY/xxxxxx/07 for a private company); download the certificate from the CIPC customer dashboard.
required_dossiers: Approved MOI as returned by CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains incorrect director details, share capital or MOI terms, file an Application for Correction or Alteration with CIPC and pay the prescribed alteration fee; if the certificate is lost, request a duplicate certificate through the eServices portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registration with SARS, Department of Employment and Labour and Sectoral Bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SARS (eFiling); Department of Employment and Labour – Compensation Fund and UIF; B-BBEE Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with SARS for Income Tax (IT), PAYE, SDL and UIF; apply for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZAR 1 million; register with the Compensation Fund under COIDA and obtain letters of good standing; submit a B-BBEE Affidavit if annual turnover is below the applicable threshold; open the corporate banking account under the First Board Resolution and bank mandate supporting Maritime Installment LC and Escrow payment rails.
required_dossiers: Director identity documents and proof of address
First Board Resolution and banking mandate
Lease or title deed of the registered office and shipyard site
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects a registration due to record mismatches or outstanding prior tax liabilities, correct the submission online and, if necessary, attend a SARS branch with the incorporation certificate; late registrations attract administrative penalties – apply for SARS Voluntary Disclosure Programme (VDP) before penalties crystallise; UIF/COIDA discrepancies are remedied via the Department of Employment and Labour employer-registration correction process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) in co-jurisdiction with the South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA), Transnet National Ports Authority (TNPA) and Municipal Fire and Building Control authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Shipbuilding Facility Operating Licence – comprising the Environmental Authorisation (NEMA EIA), Atmospheric Emission Licence (NEM:AQA) and TNPA Port Works Licence, supplemented by SAMSA vessel-construction survey approval.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – Environmental Authorisation Directorate; Delegated Provincial Environmental Authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA: Basic Assessment (Listing Notice 1, EIA Regulations 2014) for slipways, worksheds and launch-ways below thresholds; Scoping and EIA Report (Listing Notice 2) where dredging, piling, wet-berth construction or marine discharges are involved; Environmental Authorisation must be granted before construction commences.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with NEM:AQA (Act 39 of 2004) Minimum Emission Standards for abrasive blasting, coating, welding fume and diesel machinery exhaust, with facility-specific limits in the Atmospheric Emission Licence; wastewater discharges must meet the National Water Act 1998 Section 21 General Authorisation (pH 5.5-9.5, chemical oxygen demand ≤ 75 mg/l, total suspended solids ≤ 25 mg/l) and municipal sewer by-laws; waste paints, solvents, blast grit and bilge oil must be handled, stored and disposed of in accordance with NEM: Waste Act 2008 with waste manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the municipal Fire and Rescue Service; structural load inspection certificates for dry-dock, slipways, gantry cranes and buildings per SANS 10400 National Building Regulations; registration with the Department of Employment and Labour under COIDA and OHS Act 85 of 1993, including approved risk assessments and emergency response plans; TNPA port-safety clearance for yard operations adjacent to port waters.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za; physical head office at 299 Bronkhorst Street, Brooklyn, Pretoria, 0181
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity that becomes a South African resident for tax purposes, or a non-resident derived South African-source income or carrying on a South African enterprise, must: (1) apply for registration as a taxpayer via the SARS eFiling portal or at a SARS branch, completing the applicable registration forms (e.g., IT77 for income tax, VAT101 for VAT vendor registration); (2) submit supporting documents including the certificate of incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation, trust deed or partnership agreement, proof of registered office/place of business, and identification documents of directors/members; (3) SARS will issue a taxpayer reference number (income tax) and VAT number separately; non-resident companies without a fixed South African place of business must register for income tax through a SARS-appointed representative taxpayer under section 57 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; VAT registration by the 'enterprise' (Pty) Ltd is mandatory from the first day of the month following the end of a 12-month period in which taxable supplies exceeded R1 million, or voluntarily from commencement if taxable supplies will exceed R250,000 within the next 12 months; a non-resident supplier making supplies in South Africa in the course of an enterprise must also register if the threshold is met; no minimum share capital is required, but SARS requires physical presence verification and a letter of good standing from the home jurisdiction tax authority where offshore; the registration must be completed within 21 business days of the date the obligation to register arises
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A South African (Pty) Ltd is a separate taxable person subject to corporate income tax (CIT) at 27% (with a reduced rate of 21% for small business corporations meeting the turnover and shareholding criteria under section 12E of the Income Tax Act); dividends are subject to a dividend tax at 20% on distribution; capital gains are taxed at an effective CIT rate of 21.6% for the corporate (inclusion rate 80%); the entity does not automatically qualify for pass-through treatment; however, the entity may be treated as a 'controlled foreign company' (CFC) if it is a foreign-resident subsidiary of a South African resident, the ETC regime of SARS will attribute net income to the resident shareholder; section 64C re-characterisation relief applies where the CFC is a resident of a list of listed countries (including South Africa being the home jurisdiction) – the foreign business establishment (FBE) exemption under section 9D(9) applies to active trading income of a shipyard if the shipyard has a fixed place of business outside South Africa with no South African shareholder control over trading decisions; for a purely domestic SA (Pty) Ltd, no election is available to shift to pass-through or flow-through taxation; the company is taxed on its worldwide income (IFRS-based taxable income) and is subject to CFC attribution rules only for its own foreign subsidiaries
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) 'Check-the-box' equivalent: South Africa does not have a functional currency check-the-box election; however, a 'headquarters company' election under section 9I allows a South African resident company to elect to be treated as a designated group company for CFC relief, thereby exempting certain foreign dividends and interest from taxation; (2) Hybrid entity election: a foreign-incorporated entity may file an election under section 1(C) of the Income Tax Act to be treated as a South African resident if it is managed and controlled in South Africa; the 'place of effective management' test governs; (3) Small business corporation (SBC) election under section 12E: an election to apply the graduated SBC CIT rates (0% on first R95,750; 7% on next R364,250; 21% on the balance up to R550,000) allowed for a (Pty) Ltd with gross income under R20 million and less than 50% of income from investment or personal service; (4) Turnover tax election under Sixth Schedule for micro businesses with turnover under R1 million, available for non-manufacturing service companies but not available for a shipyard (shipbuilding is excluded as it falls under 'professional services' or 'manufacturing' for turnover tax purposes) – therefore a shipyard (Pty) Ltd will not be eligible for turnover tax; (5) VAT group election under section 50 of the VAT Act allows a group of companies (up to 20 members) to apply to SARS for a single VAT registration where the entities are part of the same economic unit; the election will result in a consolidated VAT return (VAT 201) and no VAT charged on intra-group supplies; (6) Cross-border branch election: a resident company with a foreign permanent establishment can elect to exclude the PE's attributable profits under section 9D(9A) where a 'foreign business establishment' is present, avoiding double taxation via an exemption election instead of a credit

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS; also subject to the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 for import VAT and ADC (Ad Valorem Customs) duties on certain goods
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration where taxable supplies (supplies made in the course of an enterprise) exceed ZAR 1,000,000 (one million rand) in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted if projected taxable supplies for the next 12 months exceed ZAR 50,000 (R50,000) but the practical minimum for a shipyard is ZAR 1 million; a non-resident supplier is required to register if it makes any supply connected with a 'South African enterprise' and total taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000; if the shipyard only exports ships (zero-rated supplies), zero-rated supplies count toward the R1 million threshold for mandatory registration, but the VAT Act permits a person whose supplies are all zero-rated to apply for a waiver from registration under section 23(3) if the person's taxable supplies consist exclusively of zero-rated supplies; nevertheless, registration is advisable for input VAT recovery on export production costs
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate a continuous transaction control (CTC) real-time fiscal clearance system (such as e-invoicing with government API clearance). However, SARS mandates the following e-invoicing and digital record requirements: (1) eFiling is the mandatory electronic channel for VAT return submission (VAT201) and customs declarations via the SARS Customs EDI / eSIE (Electronic Single Interface) system; (2) VAT invoices must be issued in an electronically authenticated format that satisfies Section 20(4) of the VAT Act – the invoice must contain all prescribed particulars: supplier name, VAT registration number, invoice date, description of goods/services, consideration (including VAT), and the wordings 'tax invoice'; (3) SARS accepts XML/UBL (Ubl 2.1) format e-invoices; an API integration via the SARS eFiling Partner API is available for large enterprise or service providers; there is no requirement for digital stamping or digital signatures with a government-issued certificate, but the use of an SEID (SARS Electronic ID) is mandatory for company representatives; (4) Real-time fiscal clearance is not operative for B2B VAT but is mandatory for the SARS Customs National Clearance System – all export shipments must obtain an electronic customs clearance declaration (SAD500) through the eSIE portal before departure from a South African port; SAD500 must be endorsed by the South African Revenue Service's Customs department (SARS Customs) prior to loading on an oceangoing vessel; SARS is in a phased rollout of e-invoicing ('e-Invoicing by SARS'), expected to mandate structured e-invoicing (PEPPOL) for large taxpayers from 2025; for the shipyard, the issuance of VAT tax invoices in compliance with section 20 is sufficient; no additional real-time clearance of tax invoices is currently required

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of movable goods (including a newly constructed ocean container vessel) from South Africa to a recipient outside South Africa, where the goods are exported by the supplier or at the supplier's direction within 90 days of the time of supply (or such longer period as SARS may allow on good cause), is zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act. The shipyard must retain proof of export (customs declaration) and proof of shipment. In the case of a ship sold, the supply constitutes a 'supply of goods' not a supply of services if title passes and the ship is physically exported by the buyer or seller. If the vessel is delivered in South Africa to a non-resident who will sail it out of South African waters, the export may be zero-rated if the ship is exported on or before the date of departure from South Africa, and the following documents are retained: (i) a commercial invoice; (ii) the bill of entry (SAD500) showing the export; (iii) the bill of lading or certificate of the Master/Port Authority confirming departure; (iv) a letter from the non-resident confirming the vessel left South Africa. Offshore services (shipbuilding engineering, design, installation, repair) supplied to a non-resident client may be zero-rated under section 11(2)(l) – 'services for moveable property that is situated in South Africa at the time of supply and is subsequently exported' – provided the vessel is a moveable and exported on or before the due date for the VAT return of the period of supply. Zero-rating of a supply of a ship to a non-resident that is subsequently registered or used as a coastal vessel in South Africa is disallowed. VAT refunds (input claims) on the costs of construction are recoverable to the extent that outputs are zero-rated or taxable at the standard rate; the refund is paid by SARS on a monthly VAT return (VAT201) within 21 business days from the date of submission if all substantiation is complete; SARS may suspend a refund if the exporter has a material audit finding or risk indicator, requiring an alternative bank guarantee for up to 100% of the refund amount for up to 18 months
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 / SAD501) endorsed by SARS Customs
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Certificate of Vessel Registration and Port of Departure Clearing Certificate

Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange (FX) confirmation showing foreign-sourced payment; for exports, a stamped Commercial Invoice and Packing List are also required; a Free on Board (FOB) or Cost, Insurance, Freight (CIF) invoice
Proof of Export: a delivery note signed by the carrier, port terminal receipt, or a Master's Receipt confirming the vessel left the exclusive economic zone (EEZ)
VAT 201 return with the zero-rating schedule (Part C) and, when the vessel is classified as a capital good, a VAT202 declaration of intended use
Copy of the shipyard's shipyard licence under the Merchant Shipping Act (National Department of Transport) where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may, within a period of 5 years from the date of the relevant VAT return (extended to 5 years for fraudulent misrepresentation and unlimited time in the case of concealment), perform a zero-rating audit on the exporter. If SARS determines that the zero-rating was applied incorrectly or that the goods were not exported within the allowed time frame, the following consequences apply: (1) the exporter is liable to account for output VAT at the standard rate (15%) on the original supply amount plus interest at the prescribed rate (currently the SARB repo rate + 7% per annum, compounded monthly); (2) an understatement penalty under Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 is payable – the 'understatement penalty' ranges from 10% (if no reasonable grounds for the incorrect position) up to 100% of the excluded tax for 'intentional tax evasion'; in addition, a penal 'substantial understatement' penalty of 50% of the VAT avoided applies if the understatement exceeds the greater of 5% of the correct tax amount or R1 million; (3) criminal charges for fraudulent claim of zero-rating or refund under section 78 of the Income Tax Act and section 58 of the VAT Act may be laid – upon conviction, a fine of up to ZAR 5 million or imprisonment of up to 5 years; (4) a 'clawback' provision applies under section 16(2) of the VAT Act: VAT that was originally claimed as an input tax credit on the export production costs may be recaptured if a subsequent event shows that the vessel remained in South Africa or was not exported, requiring the shipyard to pay output VAT equal to the input VAT previously claimed; this reclassification is treated as a separate taxable supply on the date of the recapture event; (5) the exporter may also be blocked from receiving future VAT refunds via a 'withholding of refund' until a bank guarantee is lodged; (6) SARS reporting of foreign-exchange misstatements to the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) of the South African Reserve Bank may trigger a currency control penalty of up to ZAR 1 million per occurrence and the loss of the exporter's approved status as an 'Authorised Dealer in Foreign Exchange' (if the shipyard trades directly in FX); failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days is an exchange-control contravention under the Exchange Control Regulations (1961) – the penalty is a monetary penalty of up to 10% of the outstanding amount, with no fixed cap; the 180-day deadline is measured from the date of shipment (the bill of lading date), not the date of zero-rating claim; any foreign currency invoice granted for an extended period (beyond 180 days) must be pre-approved by SARS/FinSurv; extra time extensions may be granted on application where the debtor is an offshore project finance structured entity and documentary proof of payment guarantee is supplied. Annual audit scrutiny thresholds are low: any refund claim exceeding ZAR 2 million triggers automatic segregation and an automated audit queue; SARS's 'Deliverables Review' programme mandates that a refund is either paid or refused within 21 business days from the date of filing, and this statutory deadline is temperately enforced. Overall, a shipyard must maintain a full longitudinal file (export submission, bill of lading, fixed FX contract, proof of repatriation) for 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations promulgated thereunder; authorised dealers (registered commercial banks) administer day-to-day FX controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is a managed-float, partially convertible currency. Current-account trade (imports/exports of goods and services) is freely permitted against full documentary support, with no mandatory conversion ratio imposed on export receipts; proceeds must be repatriated to South Africa but may be retained in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with a local authorised dealer. Capital-account inflows (non-resident equity subscription, shareholder loans) require authorised-dealer filing under the Balance of Payments (BOP) reporting system with a 3:1 debt/equity back-to-back loan limitation, while outbound FDI is liberalised to a ZAR1 billion per-company annual allowance. Profit remittances are permitted on a current basis subject to SARS tax clearance, a completed CMB2/remittance instruction, and statutory withholding taxes on dividends (20%) and interest (15%), potentially reduced under applicable double tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no fixed percentage conversion-to-ZAR surrender requirement; however, the full 100% of export proceeds (including stage milestone payments under maritime installment LCs) must be received by a South African authorised dealer within 30 days of the date of shipment or the relevant invoice milestone. Authorised dealers may extend this timeline upon application and full retention of proceeds in a designated Foreign Currency Account is permitted without mandatory conversion. Statutory export documentation (commercial invoice, bill of lading, customs export entry SAD500) must be retained in the exporter's exchange-control file for audit and verification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Maritime Installment LC Escrow

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail; ancillary use only. South Africa does not currently operate a European-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime, and offshore EMIs are not authorised dealers under the Exchange Control Regulations; they therefore cannot lawfully effect ZAR settlement, execute USD/ZAR conversion, or complete SARB reporting. Using an offshore EMI as the main clearing utility would create exchange-control non-compliance and documentary gaps; the shipyard should rely on SARB-authorised banks for all statutory FX flows, with EMIs confined to non-ZAR incidental fees where a registered bank remains the compliance owner.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA permits risk-based non-face-to-face onboarding, but for a foreign-owned medium-risk enhanced shipyard, South African tier-1 banks in practice require at least one physical meeting (in-country board representative or relationship-manager site visit) to verify directors and material beneficial owners. Remote opening is conditionally acceptable where the bank performs video identification augmented by notarised/legalised identity packs, a sworn source-of-funds declaration, and external legal attestation; final mandate execution is often accepted electronically, yet the bank reserves an absolute right to require in-person KYC before activating escrow flow or granting FX limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain of the foreign parent/shareholders (ownership thresholds at 25% or greater)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership register extract; corporate organisational chart evidencing ultimate natural persons; MOI and shareholder agreements; passport copies attested by a notary; source-of-wealth letter from the shareholder's home-country bank; auditor's confirmation tracing injected funds through the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and strategic-trade exposure in shipbuilding procurement (dual-use propulsion, navigation electronics, steel origin)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive UN/OFSI/OFAC/SADC sanctions screening report of all counterparties; vessel classification certificate confirming commercial ocean-container specification; end-user certificate and supplier dual-use declarations; insurance declaration evidencing lawful trade; procurement register with Incoterms for each foreign supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value advance payments flowing through maritime installment escrow and LC structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shipbuilding contract with milestone payment schedule; bank-issued or confirmed LC drafts; escrow agreement specifying disbursement conditions; pro-forma invoices and credit note trail; bank KYC reference from the buyer's confirming bank confirming the underlying commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person presence within UBO or directorate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP self-declaration; enhanced source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence (asset statements, tax returns, sale agreements); independent legal opinion confirming compliance with the FICA Code; acceptance of periodic compliance monitoring as an ongoing condition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SARS tax clearance or historical arrears impacting account activation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN (TCS); proof of provisional tax filings; fixed-asset registry including shipyard premises and dry-dock infrastructure; direct SARS eFiling transcripts; board resolution authorising SARS remediation where arrears exist.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity subscription must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the shipyard's designated authorised-dealer account with BOP code 3610 ('Inward Direct Investment – Equity Capital') in the payment narrative. The authorised dealer opens a corporate exchange-control file, verifies the funds against the share subscription agreement, board allotment resolution and CIPC notice of share issue, then credits proceeds to a ZAR operational account or a USD-denominated FCA as elected by the company. Release of inward funds is immediate upon documentation; the bank then files the inward BOP report and the company updates its CIPC/UBO registers. For any shareholder loan component, a formal loan agreement, board approval, and debt-to-equity ratio compliance (3:1 maximum for capitalisation) are required to avoid deemed-dividend treatment on later repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Procurement of steel, engines, electronics and ship components from foreign suppliers settles via SWIFT MT103 against the import documentation set (commercial invoice, ocean/air waybill, SAD500 import customs entry, packing list and insurance certificate) under BOP import code 4210. For large-ticket or repetitive maritime procurement, the shipyard's ZA bank issues Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) confirmed by the supplier's bank, or utilises Bank Payment Undertakings (BPU) and documentary collections, with sight/term tenors aligned to the shipbuilding milestone schedule. Local ZAR disbursements (payroll, utilities, subcontractors) clear through the National Payment System (NPS) via SAMOS/PCH; intra-group services and royalties are batched monthly with corresponding BOP codes and SARS source documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/ZAR Deliverable Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) with a SARB authorised dealer, backed by firm commercial shipbuilding and procurement exposures
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-term vessel financing and installment LC drawdowns against USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR movements
Vanilla USD/ZAR FX options (calls and puts) capped at the underlying trade exposure, with authorised-dealer confirmation and no naked speculative use
JSE-listed USD/ZAR FX futures and options contracts providing exchange-traded hedging for treasury risk management

Structured multi-leg hedges are permitted where economically linked to the shipyard's documented commercial cash flows; offshore USD/ZAR NDFs are not permissible for a resident ZA entity without specific FinSurv approval because ZAR is deliverable in the onshore market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation (CIPC registration date); a company registered on a specific anniversary date must file by the 30th business day thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts CIPC late-return penalties (approximately ZAR 200–500 per overdue year, escalating per year overdue) and a formal compliance notice; two consecutive years of default trigger suspension of registration and administrative strike-off; directors may be personally liable for company debts contracted during suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (including shareholding transfer declarations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual return within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial interest must additionally be declared to CIPC within 10 business days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm beneficial ownership or to report changes is a statutory breach under the Companies Act 2008 read with the anti-money-laundering amendments; CIPC may issue a compliance notice, and persistent default may lead to court-ordered deregistration; directors who knowingly submit false beneficial ownership data are subject to fines or imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and Annual Financial Statements (AFS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the financial year (e.g., a 31 December year-end return is due no later than 31 December of the following year); the audited AFS must be prepared within 6 months after the financial year-end and tabled for shareholder approval under the Companies Act 2008.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS imposes an administrative non-compliance penalty of up to 10% of assessed tax per month of default (capped at 100% of assessed tax) plus prescribed-rate interest on underpaid tax; continued default may result in an additional assessment, tax judgment, and attachment of company assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit arises under the Companies Act 2008, s 30 and Regulations 28 where the Public Interest Score (PI Score) equals or exceeds 350; PI Score 100–349 requires an independent review; PI Score below 100 is exempt from both unless the Memorandum of Incorporation requires otherwise. PI Score is driven by turnover, employee count, shareholder interests, and third-party debt; a commercial shipyard manufacturing deep-sea container vessels will ordinarily exceed 350 and therefore be subject to a mandatory statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in South Africa, or IFRS for SMEs for qualifying private companies; the South African Statements of GAAP have been withdrawn; the Memorandum of Incorporation may impose full IFRS irrespective of size.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 2008 and subsequent beneficial-ownership amendments, the company must maintain a Beneficial Interest Register and confirm the accuracy of its beneficial ownership information to CIPC during each annual return cycle. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial control must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days, and the annual confirmation must reflect the updated pattern of control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Preferential rates and deductions include the 15% corporate rate for approved Special Economic Zone (SEZ) entities; accelerated capital allowances under s 12C on manufacturing plant and equipment (40% first-year allowance and 20% per year thereafter for qualifying manufacture); an additional 50% deduction for qualifying research and development under s 11D; s 12I industrial policy investment allowances; and s 12H learnership allowances. Commercial shipbuilding qualifies as a process of manufacture for these allowances where the criteria are met.
